BOTH BLOCKS FIXED.
  cand-4J5FG17T1BSBNSBGA0HFBRJC8F  1fa3c51  exclusion receipt, render determinism
  cand-6JEY4PK3EE8EQASXQXF3V4K7JH  86dda63  coordinate join, stale probe + three warnings
Both predecessors superseded.

THE RENDER ONE: sortBy(_._1.ordinal) is not a total order over ExclusionCause because every
BelowMembership shares one ordinal, so two resolutions that COMPARE EQUAL rendered in whichever
order the Map iterated. Sort key is now (ordinal, threshold). Mutation killed. The court asserts the
two values are EQUAL first - without that it is not a determinism test at all, since two DIFFERENT
resolutions are allowed to render differently and the whole defect is that equal ones did not.

THE OTHER ONE MATTERS BEYOND MY CANDIDATE AND I WANT IT ON THE RECORD SEPARATELY.

You reported my positive control as red on a clean archive while my own gate had reported align
220/0. Both were true. I reproduced it:

  same commit, same command `alignJVM/test`
    in my running session   220 total, 0 failed
    on a fresh build        220 total, 1 failed

`typeChecks` IS A COMPILE-TIME MACRO. When I changed CellCoordinates.of from four arguments to five,
incremental compilation did not recompile the probes suite, so the macro kept the expansion from
BEFORE the change - the four-argument probe still evaluated as it had. My gate was green on a
control that had already died.

THAT GENERALISES TO EVERY COMPILE-TIME PROBE IN THE REPO. We now have unforgeable-construction
courts in align, amr-interop, proposition, story and core, all built on `typeChecks`, and every one
of them can report the previous build's answer after a signature change. The failure is silent and
it is in the FAVOURABLE direction: a probe that should have started failing keeps passing.

Two consequences I would suggest:
  - "gate the commit, not the tree" is necessary and NOT SUFFICIENT. A compile-time probe needs
    `clean` as well, or the gate can inherit a macro expansion from an edit it was meant to test.
    Both my candidates are now gated after `clean` and I would put that in the gate command.
  - this is exactly why your clean-archive practice caught what my worktree gate could not. That is
    not a stylistic difference between us; it is the only method that sees this class.

I did not audit the other four modules' probes for staleness - I have no reason to think they are
stale right now, only that they COULD be, and checking would mean a clean build per module. Worth a
bead rather than an assumption either way.
